weaknesses: The size of the constants behind the "matched minimax" claim is never disclosed, and a reader cannot recover it without reading the proof. In the proof of \cref{obj:thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}, step 1, the upper constant is proportional to $\underline a^{-2}=2^{2\overline u_\star}$ with $\overline u_\star\gtrsim \overline N_{\mathrm{cert}}^2$ and $\overline N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4\overline U_\psi^2(\overline U_R+2)^3$, while $R_1$ itself carries the factor $A_k=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)}$; the resulting $C$ is a tower in $(\delta,\psi_\eta,r)$, and $c$ is $O(1)$. Add a remark immediately after the theorem (and one clause in the abstract, e.g. "of order $n^{-1}$ with constants depending on the fixed primitives through the contour-bank certificate") stating that the two matched constants are not of comparable magnitude and giving the explicit dependence of $C$ on $a_\star$ and $R_1$.

The treatment-code gate $\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\{4R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\}^{-1}$ is presented in the abstract and \cref{obj:thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax} only as "sufficiently small," but with $R_1=A_k(\psi_\eta^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}+1$ this threshold is exponentially small in the primitives, and the interesting separation regime of \cref{obj:prop:jms-ace-alignment} (where $(\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}+C_\theta\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1})/n^{-1/2}\to\infty$) requires the radii to stay bounded away from zero, so the ACE bound has a floor while the contour bound vanishes. Add a paragraph in the comparison section spelling out this regime explicitly ("the separation obtains when the supplied codes do not improve with $n$, so the finite-order ACE bound is bounded below while the contour bound is $O((\gamma n)^{-1/2})$") and give the numerical order of the admissible $\varepsilon_{1,n}$ for a concrete $(\delta,\psi_\eta,r)$.

The independence restriction \cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise} is motivated only as "the standard residual-independence restriction" in the sentence following it, with no discussion of what it excludes. Combined with \cref{obj:ass:cumulant-separation} it rules out binary and other discrete treatments, i.e. the leading applied partially linear design, since $\eta=T-g_0(X)$ with $T\in\{0,1\}$ can be independent of $X$ only when $g_0$ is constant. Extend that paragraph (and the limitations section) to state the exclusion affirmatively: name the treatment designs the construction covers (continuous treatments with covariate-free innovation and a separated cumulant, e.g. the mixture and Gaussian--Rademacher benchmarks of the mixture section) and say plainly that discrete-treatment designs fall outside the class.

All Gaussian-benchmark conclusions are conditional on a nonemptiness hypothesis that the paper never examines. \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} imposes $|Y|\le C_q$, $\eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$, and the exact partially linear mean simultaneously, and \cref{obj:prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy} shows every member has $\theta_0(P)=0$; the risk equalities then hold "whenever the fixed-code intersection is nonempty," which is never verified. Add one sentence to the paragraph after \cref{obj:prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy} exhibiting a member (e.g. $Y=q_0(X)+\xi$ with bounded $q_0$ and bounded $\xi$) so the reader knows the statement is not vacuous, and soften the abstract/introduction phrase "the diagnostic Gaussian benchmark" to say that this comparison class identifies a degenerate target rather than a competing estimation problem.

The executable component is stated only as a conditional contract, and no witness is ever exhibited. Both the "Represented execution" clause of \cref{obj:thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax} and the corresponding clause of \cref{obj:thm:common-experiment-dichotomy} are universally quantified over "every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build-and-compilation specification," and \cref{obj:def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate} closes with "Later executable conclusions are conditional on a compiled build satisfying this specification" -- so the abstract's "certified finite-arithmetic specification for the contour statistic" is a specification, not a demonstrated implementation. Either state in the appendix C preamble and the abstract that this layer is a specification whose discharge is left to an implementation, or record that a build discharging $\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}$ exists and cite it.

Several reader-facing artifacts and formalization leaks undercut the register of the manuscript and should be swept before circulation: the bullet labels "(Non-Gaussian fixed-code u.)" and "(ACE fixed-code u.)" in \cref{obj:thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax} and "Its mean squared u obeys" in \cref{obj:lem:gaussian-rademacher-l1-benchmark} contain a stray token where "mean-squared error" belongs; \cref{obj:def:generalized-quantile}'s trailing paragraph carries `\leanref{S-6}{of the finite i.i.d. sample}`, a non-`sym:` key rendering prose as a symbol link; the conclusion of \cref{obj:thm:exact-contour-identification} displays the coercion "$(\theta_0(P):\mathbb C)$", \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle} writes the exponent as "$s\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\infty}$", and \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} uses $X$ for the covariate space and "model records $m$"; the appendix titles "A: Proofs...", "B: ...", "C: ...", "D: ..." duplicate the letters `\appendix` already supplies; environment titles are inconsistently capitalized ("Common Experiment Dichotomy", "Zero-Free Nuisance Factor", "Local Gaussian Benchmarks" against "Known zero instrument", "Adaptive root-n minimaxity"); \cref{obj:ass:treatment-code-radius} and \cref{obj:ass:jms-treatment-code-radius} carry the identical title "Treatment code radius" (likewise the two outcome-radius assumptions), so cleveref gives the reader no way to tell them apart -- retitle them "$L^s$ treatment code radius" and "order-$r$ treatment code radius"; \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator} shouts "The integrand $V_j$ is NOT normalized at this stage"; and the final clause of \cref{obj:thm:local-to-gaussian-partial-benchmarks} ("for all real numbers $u,U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}$, if $u\le U_{\mathrm{DML}}$ and $u\le U_{\mathrm{ACE}}$, then $u\le\min\{\cdot,\cdot\}$") is a tautology that should be deleted from the theorem statement, together with its first bullet's non-statement "Then the Gaussian--Rademacher path benchmark conclusion holds with constant $C$ for $p,m,a$", which should be replaced by the displayed conclusion itself.

Abstract: the sentence saying zeros generate valid instruments after residualization compresses several gates from \cref{obj:thm:known-zero-instrument} and \cref{obj:thm:exact-contour-identification}; revise to name the known-zero multiplicity, nonzero denominator, zero-free nuisance, and positive-count conditions at first mention.

Introduction/main theorem discussion: phrases such as “matched minimax” should state “over fixed-code classes, under fixed primitive constants and the displayed treatment-code stability gate,” because the theorem is conditional on nonempty fixed-code slices and transported certified records.

Setup and related work: independent treatment noise is described mainly as standard in the JMS experiment; add a short interpretive paragraph explaining that this is a strong residual-independence structure and clarifying empirical settings where it is plausible.

Gaussian benchmark discussion: the zero-risk Gaussian result is technically clear but easy to misread as a favorable comparison; add a sentence in the benchmark paragraph saying the bounded-outcome Gaussian intersection is a diagnostic degenerate experiment rather than a substantive estimation benchmark.

Writing: several theorem bullets contain placeholder-like text such as “Non-Gaussian fixed-code u,” “ACE fixed-code u,” and “mean squared u”; replace these with polished labels such as “Non-Gaussian fixed-code risk” and “mean-squared error.”

Organization: the certified arithmetic appendix is very long relative to the statistical narrative; move implementation-level details to a shorter specification table or supplementary appendix and keep the main appendix focused on the statistic-to-risk correspondence.

The abstract and introduction assert a matched minimax rate ("attain fixed-code minimax mean-squared error of order $n^{-1}$") without the qualifier that the constants $c$ and $C$ are unrelated: the theorem gives $c/n \le \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}} \le C/n$ with $C$ built from $L_{\mathrm{fix}}$, $\underline a = 2^{-\overline u_\star}$, and $\overline u_\star$ growing like $\overline U_\psi^2 \overline U_R^3$ — i.e. $C/c$ is doubly exponential in the primitives. The abstract's line about "asymmetric magnitudes" gestures at this but understates it. Fix: in the abstract and in the paragraph after \cref{obj:thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}, state plainly that the result is a rate characterization in $n$ with the constant ratio depending super-exponentially on $(\psi_\eta, R_1)$ through $a_\star = 2^{-u_\star}$, so the bracket is not a sharp-constant statement.

The paper never confronts the fact that the fixed-code minimax bracket in \cref{obj:thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax} is proved on a class whose lower bound comes from a two-point family that varies only $\theta_0$ while holding the $(X,T)$-law, $g_0$, $q_0$, and both clipped codes fixed (\cref{obj:lem:non-gaussian-hard-submodel}). Under that construction the $c/n$ lower bound is essentially the parametric bound for a one-dimensional Gaussian location problem, so the 'matched' claim is much weaker than a genuine semiparametric efficiency statement — in particular it says nothing about whether the contour estimator's constant is near the semiparametric efficiency bound. Fix: add two sentences after \cref{obj:lem:non-gaussian-hard-submodel} stating what the lower bound does and does not establish, and remove or qualify 'matched' in the introduction.

The $L^1(P_X)$ treatment-code gate $\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\{4R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\}^{-1}$ is presented as a mild stability condition, but its restrictiveness is never quantified: $R_1 = A_k(\psi_\eta^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}+1$ with $A_k=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)}$, so for weak separation or moderate $k$ the admissible radius is exponentially small, and it is a fixed-$n$ threshold rather than a rate condition — meaning the theorem can be vacuous for any realistic first-stage learner at moderate $n$. Fix: in the setup discussion after \cref{obj:ass:l1-treatment-code-radius}, add a worked numerical illustration (e.g. $k=4$, $\psi_\eta=1$, $\delta=1$) giving the implied bound on $\varepsilon_{1,n}$, and say explicitly which nuisance-estimation regimes satisfy it.

The ACE comparison is described as an 'upper-guarantee comparison' in several places, but the framing in the introduction ('the displayed contour upper guarantee is asymptotically smaller') and the Related work paragraph ('the contour guarantee is governed by the fixed zero geometry while the finite-order ACE bound retains its explicit dependence on the nuisance radii') still reads as a claim about procedures rather than about two published inequalities. The separation is driven entirely by the fact that the contour bound has no nuisance-radius term inside its stated gate, and no attempt is made to argue the ACE bound is tight. Fix: in the introduction paragraph on higher-order orthogonal learning and in the discussion after \cref{obj:prop:jms-ace-alignment}, state once that no lower bound is available for the ACE procedure, so the comparison cannot distinguish a genuine procedural gap from slack in the published ACE bound.

The residual-independence assumption $\eta \perp X$ (\cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise}) is the binding design restriction of the whole paper, yet its discussion is one paragraph in Related work and the accompanying justification is thin: 'plausible in randomized or engineered assignment settings' is asserted without a concrete empirical design, and the discrete-treatment exclusion is noted but not developed. Fix: expand the setup discussion after \cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise} with at least one named applied design where a continuous treatment shock is credibly independent of covariates (not merely mean-independent), and state what fails when independence is weakened to conditional-mean independence — specifically that $F_n = M H_n$ no longer factors, which breaks \cref{obj:lem:observable-factorization} and hence the entire contour argument.

Sections C and the certified-construction material occupy a large fraction of the paper (\cref{obj:def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate,obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator} run to many pages of interval-arithmetic and mesh-fuel bookkeeping) while contributing nothing to the statistical claims, and the abstract concedes the executable discharge is 'an implementation obligation' — so the layer is specified but not realized. For an econometrics readership this inverts the expected weighting. Fix: compress \cref{obj:def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate} to a half-page statement of the contract (records, guarded division, mesh rule, soundness and modulus exports) with the algorithmic detail moved to a supplement, and state in one sentence at the head of Appendix C that no compiled adapter is exhibited here.

Several notational and copy-editing defects would be flagged at a journal: the theorem clause labels '(Non-Gaussian fixed-code u.)' and '(ACE fixed-code u.)' in \cref{obj:thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax} and 'Its mean squared u obeys' in \cref{obj:lem:gaussian-rademacher-l1-benchmark} appear to be corrupted text; \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} carries no title while every sibling definition does; the setup introduces $a\lesssim b$ but the symbol is never used; and \cref{obj:def:local-gaussian-handle} writes the radii sequences as $\epsilon_{1n},\epsilon_{2n}$ where the rest of the paper uses $\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}$. Fix: repair the three corrupted clause labels, title \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}, drop the unused $\lesssim$ convention, and unify the radius notation.

Several headings and theorem titles violate the sentence-case typography rule, e.g. “Common Experiment Dichotomy,” “Local Gaussian Benchmarks,” and “Zero-Free Nuisance Factor”; change them to sentence case such as “Common experiment dichotomy,” “Local Gaussian benchmarks,” and “Zero-free nuisance factor.”

The main theorem contains visible placeholder/typo text in reader-facing labels: “Non-Gaussian fixed-code u,” “ACE fixed-code u,” and later “mean squared u”; replace these with “Non-Gaussian fixed-code upper bound,” “ACE fixed-code upper bound,” and “mean squared error.”

The generalized lower quantile criterion is easy to misread as a high-probability guarantee, especially because the prose says “probability level” and compares to ACE quantiles; add a short interpretive sentence near the definition explaining that this is the lower (1-γ) quantile with γ>1/2, and preserve that wording in all comparisons.

The assumption discussion motivates residual independence but gives less economic interpretation for the population L1 treatment-code gate and the certified denominator/zero-free conditions; add a paragraph in Setup or before the main theorem explaining when these gates are plausible and how restrictive they are.

The certified-construction appendix is much more implementation-contract heavy than the econometric argument needs; add a short roadmap paragraph before Appendix C telling readers which parts are needed for measurability/executability versus the statistical rate result.

Some claims about “same kind of cumulant-separated residual variation” and ACE alignment could be read as methodological equivalence; tighten the comparison prose to say the procedures are compared only through their published upper guarantees on the common fixed-code class under both sets of gates.
